messages:
jamie: FYI customer is pushing for BYO-HSM but wants us to ingest audit telemetry for SLA reasons. question: what can we reasonably accept without crossing custody boundaries?

sam: do we have a written boundary doc for telemetry yet? i know we said 'minimal' on onboarding but not specifics. :thinking_face:

priya: we don't want key material leaving the HSM. telemetry should be operational metadata only: timestamps, op type, status, request_id, duration, operator_id (masked). no key IDs that resolve to key material.

ben: agreed. we also need to decide if HSM health metrics (temp, firmware version) are allowed in hosted ingest. customers sometimes object to hardware fingerprints.

nate: from infra side, we can accept logs over a TLS mut-auth channel and store in a customer-specific S3 in their VPC. that keeps custody in their control. we currently route logs to our central ELK; would need a flag to change to customer-vpc.

lauren: legal/compliance asked about retention windows for auditable events. some regs require 7 years, others less. are we offering configurable retention per-customer?

jamie: not yet universally. we have per-customer retention in roadmap but default is 90d. need to capture ask.

priya: two compliance requirements to call out: (1) audit trail immutability for key operations, (2) access audit showing which operator/principal requested unwrap/usage. both must be tamper-evident.

ben: tamper-evident = write-once object store + signed chain-of-events ideally. can't sign with customer key if it never leaves HSM, but we can log HMACs derived inside HSM and emit only the HMACs + event metadata. that gives integrity proof without exposing key.

sam: can you sketch payload shape? i.e. what fields we accept in ingest and which we sanitize/remove.

ben: rough proposal: 
```
{
  ts: <epoch>,
  op: "encrypt|decrypt|import|export|wrap|unwrap|rotate",
  status: "ok|fail",
  request_id: <uuid>,
  actor: <service/principal tag>,
  actor_domain: <masked tenant id>,
  hmac: <base64>,
  firmware: <major.minor> (optional),
  hw_id: <hash256 of serial>
}
```
we hash serials so no raw serial leaves. we don't accept any part of private key or key shares.

priya: important: operator_id must be an auditable principal id, not an email. PII rules. mask or pseudonymize accordingly.

nate: devops-bot created ticket INF-1245 to add customer-vpc log sink option. ops-bot also notes: please add runbook for oncall if telemetry shows HSM firmware drift.

lauren: for contracts team: we need a clause that we will not request escrow of customer keys, and telemetry will be limited to metadata hashes only. will provide sample retention options: 90d, 1yr, 7yr.

jamie: next steps: ben to draft acceptable telemetry schema + sanitization rules, nate to prototype vpc-sink, lauren to draft contract language, priya to stub compliance checklist. can we aim EOW for a sync doc? :calendar: 

ben: i'll put a PR with schema and a small sanitizer patch. linking test vectors in the PR.

nate: prototyping today, will push demo to customer sandbox by mid-week.

priya: i'll assemble a checklist with mappings to SOC2 controls and one PCI note about logging retention.

lauren: will work with sales/customer legal to add opt-in checkbox in onboarding flow.

sam: thanks all. once docs/PRs exist let's do a 30min sync and record decisions in runbook. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: INCIDENT-OP NOTE: if HSM telemetry stops for >5m for a customer with active SLAs, page oncall.

devops-bot: INFO: created branch feature/byo-hsm-telemetry in infra-logs repo.
